segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or cross a highway
from a private way
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on such highway.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (definitions table); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', claimed by its id and never expanded. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is no aggregate: ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for ... a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle', so the role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

The entry onto or across the highway is where the subject's footprint comes onto its roadway: rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, ...)'; st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' ties that roadway to the highway; st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' carries DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'. st.highway's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: the roadway') is respected: the roadway is its own atom, the highway only anchors it. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a moving entry from a vehicle standing at the edge. 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement itself (ontology, what is not an atom).

DEF-NRS-484A-190: a private way is 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel by the owner'. st.driveway_or_alley_entrance is a 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there' is why the rule adds st.alley ('a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'): an alley is a highway (DEF-NRS-484A-015 'Alley means a highway'), not a private way, so the subject must overlap the entrance and no alley region. rel.occupies anchors both to the subject's footprint.

Mapping index: 'shall yield' maps to kin.speed, rel.contact. The yield is judged while the subject moves (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above the halt tolerance): a subject at rest grants precedence. rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' is a failure to yield; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' is respected, since the near conflict is the operationalization of s5.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'on such highway' singles out the highway the subject enters: the other vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane ..., a roadway ..., a shoulder, or an intersection') lying (st.on_way) on that same highway region, re-bound with the selection of s2. st.travel_region's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the extent of a highway' is respected: the highway is read through st.on_way, the travel region only locates the vehicle. 'approaching': the vehicle moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) and the subject lies ahead of it, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame' with a positive longitudinal component.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: under constant velocities (direction and speed of both), the two centres reach their closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance; such a pair is in danger of a crash unless the subject grants precedence

applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its footprint overlaps both a roadway region r lying on a highway region h and a driveway_or_alley_entrance region e, and overlaps no alley region; its overlap with e has held at every observation since one at which it overlapped e and did not overlap r (the subject came onto the entrance from off the roadway: formula 'since').
obligation: For every selection of h, r and e satisfying the applicability's conditions at this observation (re-bound in full): for every other road user v of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps a travel region lying on h, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact (rel.contact), and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

'about to enter or cross' is an imminent movement, read by the entering movement itself: the rule judges every observation at which the moving subject straddles the private way's entrance and a roadway of the highway, having come onto the entrance from off the roadway; the rest of a crossing is judged through the closest approach under constant velocities that each such observation predicts

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle rolls out of a driveway entrance region onto roadway r of highway h, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, overlapping no alley. Vehicle v moves in a lane on h with the subject ahead of it (rel.bearing longitudinal positive); prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance is below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but v is far up the lane: their closest approach does not fall within p.conflict_horizon, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives along roadway r of h and its footprint never overlaps a driveway_or_alley_entrance region; v approaches from behind.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.bearing is not observed on the source, so whether v approaches the subject is unknown while the closest approach is a conflict.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject rolls out of a driveway entrance onto roadway r of h and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject comes out of an alley: its footprint overlaps an st.alley region and the entrance region as it reaches roadway r, with v in conflict as in forbid. An alley is a highway, not a private way.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'Driver' is a relational role (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for ... who drives or controls a vehicle'), read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

DEF-NRS-484A-060: a controlled-access highway is one 'to or from which owners or occupants of abutting lands and other persons have no legal right of access except at such points only'. st.controlled_access is 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes', and rel.occupies lists the 'controlled-access lane' among the regions a footprint overlaps. The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps a controlled-access region c having not overlapped it at the previous observation; the exit, the observation at which it does not overlap c having overlapped it at the previous one. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells the moving entry or exit. 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement itself.

Mapping index: 'shall yield' maps to kin.speed, rel.contact. The subject yields while it moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' is a failure to yield, and its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' is respected: the near conflict is the operationalization of a5.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'on the highway' is the controlled-access highway the subject enters or exits: the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the same region c of st.controlled_access, re-bound with the selection of a2. 'approaching': the vehicle moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) and the subject lies ahead of it, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame' with a positive longitudinal component.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: under constant velocities the two centres reach their closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance; a vehicle so placed is an immediate hazard

applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and there is a controlled-access region c such that at this observation the subject's footprint overlaps c and did not at the previous observation (entry: rises of rel.occupies), or does not overlap c and did at the previous observation (exit: rises of its negation).
obligation: For every region c whose entry or exit occurs at this observation (re-bound with that selection): for every other road user v of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps c, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact, and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'about to enter or exit' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into or the exit from the controlled-access region as the source maps it: the duty is judged at the observation the subject's footprint comes onto or leaves that region; where the source maps the entrance and exit lanes inside the region, the entry is judged where those lanes begin, since the ontology carries no attribute telling an entrance lane from a through lane

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint comes to overlap controlled-access region c (it did not at the previous observation), kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. Vehicle v moves on c with the subject ahead of it; prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance is below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but v is far behind on c: the closest approach does not fall within p.conflict_horizon, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject travels within c throughout: its overlap with c neither begins nor ends during the trace.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.bearing is not observed, so whether v approaches the subject is unknown while the closest approach is a conflict.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters c and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint ceases to overlap c (exit) while a vehicle v moving on c, with the subject ahead of it, is in a closest-approach conflict with the subject.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'Driver' is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

As in NRS_484B_263_o1: st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'); rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... controlled-access lane ...)'. The entry is the rise of the subject's overlap with region c, the exit the rise of its absence after overlap; kin.speed tells the subject still moves. 'About to' is read by the movement itself.

'that traffic' refers back to these words, so they keep their full qualification here: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; a footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) the same controlled-access region c; moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), with the subject ahead in its frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive).

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'); 'that traffic' is the approaching vehicles of a4, so a road user the duty concerns carries both aggregates. The continuing yield is read like the yield (mapping index 'shall yield': kin.speed, rel.contact): while the subject moves, no contact (rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)', not a stand-in for a near miss, which a5 and a7 carry). 'continue' places the duty after the entry or exit, read on the clock (kin.time 'instant of observation') through the time since that event.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard (the traffic the continuing yield concerns)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance

operationalizations.standard: until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety
operationalizations.convention: the subject may proceed with reasonable safety once no approaching vehicle of that traffic is in a traffic-conflict (closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold below the collision clearance); the continuing duty is read over the merge or diverge that follows the entry or exit, whose duration is the time an acceleration or deceleration lane is run

applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and there is a controlled-access region c whose latest entry or exit by the subject (the latest rise of the subject's overlap with c, or of its non-overlap with c after overlapping it) lies strictly before this observation and no more than p.merge_window before it (Term.sinceRise of that event above zero and at most p.merge_window).
obligation: For every such region c (re-bound with that selection): for every other road user v of the traffic aggregate and of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps c, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact, and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'about to enter or exit' is read by the entry into or exit from the controlled-access region as the source maps it, as in NRS_484B_263_o1

the continuing yield is judged at the observations that follow the entry or exit within the merge window; once that window has run the subject is taken to have merged or diverged, and its later conduct is judged by the following and lane rules, not by this one
'reasonable safety' is read through the same traffic-conflict bound as the immediate hazard: the subject may proceed once no approaching vehicle of that traffic is in such a conflict with it

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered controlled-access region c a short time ago (within p.merge_window, after the entry observation) and keeps moving; vehicle v (traffic and vehicle aggregates) moves on c with the subject ahead of it and their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but every vehicle on c is far behind: no closest approach within p.conflict_horizon, no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered c long before, more than p.merge_window ago, and travels within it; v closes from behind.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.bearing is not observed, so whether v approaches the subject is unknown while the closest approach is a conflict.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Within p.merge_window after its entry into c, the subject moves and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

segmentation.text: Upon the immediate approach of
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency,
making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of every other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Yield
the right-of-way.

elements.justification: 'authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate', never expanded. Its exclusion of a role described by conduct is respected: the conduct the words require (flashing lights, immediate approach) is carried by u4 and u1, not by the class.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency (DEF-NRS-484A-205: an agency 'granted police or enforcement powers'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' is respected: the emergency vehicle is u2's aggregate.

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour in {red, blue, amber, white}, mode in {flashing, rotating, steady}, facing in {front, rear, side}'. The requirements quoted from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', give the lamp the approaching vehicle makes use of: lit, colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an audible warning' is respected: no siren is required by these words.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'every other' excludes the approaching vehicle itself (the two variables do not denote the same road user). 'driver' is a relational role (ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for who controls a vehicle), read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Mapping index: 'the driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region. dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role in {police_officer, ...}', read with role police_officer; dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a position' respected since it only ties the officer to the subject's region; rel.occupies anchors the subject on a travel region (st.travel_region) the officer governs.

Mapping index: 'shall yield' maps to kin.speed, rel.contact. The subject yields to the approaching vehicle while it moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)' is a failure to yield, not a stand-in for a near miss, which u9 carries.

operationalizations.standard: the immediate approach of the emergency or regulatory vehicle
operationalizations.convention: the vehicle approaches: it moves (speed above the speed resolution) with the subject ahead of it in its own frame; the approach is immediate within the centre distance a vehicle at an urban response speed covers in the time a driver needs to perceive its lamps and begin clearing the way

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

applicability: There is a road user e, not the subject, that is of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, and is in immediate approach of the subject: e moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), the subject lies ahead of e in e's frame (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from e to the subject positive), and their centre distance is at most p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach. And no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps.
obligation: For every such e: where the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), the subject and e are not in contact, and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Ambulance e (authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate) with a lit red flashing front warning lamp moves toward the subject from behind within p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach, the subject ahead of it. The subject keeps moving in e's path: their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the subject has moved to the right lane: no closest approach within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance, no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e approaches as in forbid but its warning lamps are off (no lit sig.warning_lamp).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed on the source, so whether e makes use of the required lamps is unknown while the subject is in conflict with it.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a police officer (dev.human_direction, role police_officer) governs the lane the subject occupies and directs it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: An official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency with a lit red flashing front lamp approaches as in forbid and the subject's body touches it (rel.contact).

param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which an emergency or enforcement vehicle closing on a road user with its warning lamps flashing is in immediate approach: about five seconds of travel at an urban response speed of 20 m/s, the time a driver needs to perceive the lamps and begin to clear the way

segmentation.text: Upon the immediate approach of
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency,
making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of every other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph,
immediately
drive to a position parallel to, and
as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or, if applicable, curb of a highway
and clear of any intersection.
The driver shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway
where lawfully placed signage allows a vehicle described in paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210 [list appended below] to drive on the shoulder.

The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus, that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The conduct the words require of it is carried by u4 and u1, not by the class.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning, which is not required.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'every other' excludes the approaching vehicle; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic ...; role in {police_officer, ...}' read with role police_officer, governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph' refers to the paragraph's own provision that the driver 'shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows' listed vehicles 'to drive on the shoulder': the position this node requires excludes such a shoulder. st.shoulder 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic; paved attribute', read paved; dev.regulatory_sign 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... shoulder_use_permitted', governing (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or shoulder') that shoulder; rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint.

'a position parallel to' the edge: the subject's heading (kin.heading 'direction the body points') is parallel, in either sense, to the designated direction (st.lane_direction 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of a travel region (st.travel_region) its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); the carrier's direction runs along its edge. st.travel_region's exclusion of the highway's extent is respected: it only selects the carrier the subject is on.

'clear of any intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) no st.intersection region ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line' is respected.

operationalizations.standard: the immediate approach of the emergency or regulatory vehicle
operationalizations.convention: the vehicle moves with the subject ahead of it in its own frame, within the centre distance a vehicle at an urban response speed covers in the time a driver needs to perceive its lamps and begin clearing the way

the position is reached within a perception-reaction time plus the lane changes a pull-over takes, counted from the onset of the immediate approach; the duty to clear the way ends once the approaching vehicle has passed the subject (the subject behind it in its frame, their projections sharing no length)

operationalizations.standard: as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of a highway
operationalizations.convention: curb-parking clearance: a vehicle pulled over to the edge stands with its body within the curb clearance of a parked car plus lane-keeping variability of the right-hand curb or roadway edge, or on an unsigned paved shoulder beyond it

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

applicability: For some road user e, not the subject, the trigger rises at this observation (it holds here and did not at the previous observation): e is of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject ahead of it in its frame (rel.bearing longitudinal positive), within centre distance p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach. And no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: For every e whose trigger rises here: at some observation within p.emergency_pullover_window ahead (formula 'within', time), either e has passed the subject (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from e to the subject negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap of e and the subject negative), or the subject is at the position: (a) for some travel region t its footprint overlaps, the absolute dot product of its heading and t's designated direction is at least p.curb_parallel_cos; (b) for some highway h on which a travel region the subject occupies lies, either there is a road_edge region g lying on h with the ground distance from the subject's body to g (st.region_geometry) at most p.pullover_edge_gap and prim.region_lateral_offset of g from the subject at most zero (the edge on its right or under it), or the subject's footprint overlaps a paved shoulder lying on h; (c) its footprint overlaps no intersection region; (d) its footprint overlaps no paved shoulder governed by a regulatory sign of code shoulder_use_permitted.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

the duty is judged at the onset of the immediate approach; it is met once the position is reached within the window or the approaching vehicle has passed the subject first, since the paragraph's purpose, clearing its way, is then spent

'the right-hand edge ... of a highway' is read as the curb or roadway edge (st.road_edge) on the subject's right or a paved shoulder beyond it, not the outer boundary of the public way beyond the sidewalk; 'as close as possible' is read through a fixed gap, so what makes the edge unreachable (parked vehicles, obstructions) is not read
'parallel' is read with the heading in either sense along the occupied carrier's designated direction

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The trigger rises: ambulance e with a lit red flashing front lamp comes within p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach behind the moving subject. Over the next p.emergency_pullover_window the subject stays in the left lane, far from any road_edge region, and e does not pass it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: At the trigger's rise the subject moves right and, within p.emergency_pullover_window, its body is within p.pullover_edge_gap of the right road_edge (prim.region_lateral_offset negative), heading parallel to its lane's direction within p.curb_parallel_cos, overlapping no intersection and no signed shoulder.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e approaches with its warning lamps off: the trigger never rises.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the trigger rose is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Within the window the subject reaches the right edge, parallel, but its footprint overlaps an intersection region at every such observation, and e has not passed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: e overtakes and passes the subject (the subject behind e, no longitudinal overlap) before the subject reaches the edge, within p.emergency_pullover_window.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: Within the window the subject moves onto a paved shoulder governed by a shoulder_use_permitted regulatory sign and stays there; it is never at the roadway edge off that shoulder, and e has not passed.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which an emergency or enforcement vehicle closing on a road user with its warning lamps flashing is in immediate approach: about five seconds of travel at an urban response speed of 20 m/s, the time a driver needs to perceive the lamps and begin to clear the way
param_proposals.source: driver-response studies of emergency-vehicle encounters (perception-reaction time plus lane-change time)

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_pullover_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest time from the onset of an emergency vehicle's immediate approach until a driver has moved to the right-hand edge: a perception-reaction time of about 1.5 s plus one or two lane changes of about 4 s each
param_proposals.source: AASHTO perception-reaction time; naturalistic lane-change duration studies

param_proposals.name: p.pullover_edge_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between a vehicle body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which a vehicle pulled over to clear the way counts as as close to the edge as it can be placed: the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car (about 0.3 m) plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin
param_proposals.source: curb-parking clearance conventions of municipal codes and driver manuals

param_proposals.name: p.curb_parallel_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about fourteen degrees) between a stopped bus's heading and its carrier's designated direction, in either sense, at which the bus counts as approximately parallel to the curb
param_proposals.source: heading resolution of parked-vehicle placement

segmentation.text: Upon the immediate approach of
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency,
making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of every other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph,
immediately
drive to a position parallel to, and
as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or, if applicable, curb of a highway
and clear of any intersection.
The driver shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway
where lawfully placed signage allows a vehicle described in paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210 [list appended below] to drive on the shoulder.

The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus, that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'; conduct carried by u4 and u1.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'every other' excludes the approaching vehicle; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; read with role police_officer governing a travel region the subject occupies.

'drive to and stop': the subject comes to rest, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement', DEF-NRS-484A-255, the definition of 'stop' when required, here the stop the words forbid in a place) holding at this observation and not at the previous one; 'in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway': its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.shoulder region ('the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic; paved attribute') with paved attribute, lying (st.on_way) on a highway region (st.highway 'the entire public way ... including sidewalks and shoulders').

'lawfully placed signage allows ... to drive on the shoulder': dev.regulatory_sign 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... shoulder_use_permitted', governing (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — ... or shoulder') the shoulder of b6. Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a manoeuvre or a road feature' is respected: the sign is read as the condition, the shoulder is its own atom. 'lawfully placed' is the sign's status, read by its presence.

The appended list (NRS 484B.210(4)) describes the vehicles ('(a) An authorized emergency vehicle ... (f) A public transit motor bus') that 'lawfully placed signage allows ... to use the shoulder': it is the legend of the shoulder_use_permitted regulatory sign b7 reads (dev.regulatory_sign, 'with the same structured conditions attribute ... a class'). The subject's duty does not depend on its own class, so the listed classes are read only as what the sign allows.

operationalizations.standard: the immediate approach of the emergency or regulatory vehicle
operationalizations.convention: the vehicle moves with the subject ahead of it in its own frame, within the centre distance a vehicle at an urban response speed covers in the time a driver needs to perceive its lamps and begin clearing the way

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

applicability: There is a road user e, not the subject, of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, showing a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject ahead of it in its frame (rel.bearing longitudinal positive), within centre distance p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach; and no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: It is not the case that the subject comes to rest at this observation (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance holds here and did not at the previous observation) while its footprint overlaps a shoulder region with paved attribute, lying on a highway region, that a regulatory sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governs.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'lawfully placed signage' is read by the sign's presence governing the shoulder

'drive to and stop' is read as the subject coming to rest on such a shoulder while the emergency vehicle's immediate approach lasts; a vehicle already at rest there before the approach began is not judged

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Ambulance e with a lit red flashing front lamp approaches the moving subject within p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach; the subject pulls onto a paved shoulder governed by a shoulder_use_permitted regulatory sign and comes to rest there (complete_halt rises).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the subject comes to rest at the roadway edge with its footprint off that shoulder.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No vehicle with lit warning lamps approaches; the subject stops on the signed shoulder.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the duty is engaged is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the paved shoulder carries no shoulder_use_permitted sign: stopping there is allowed.

param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which an emergency or enforcement vehicle closing on a road user with its warning lamps flashing is in immediate approach: about five seconds of travel at an urban response speed of 20 m/s, the time a driver needs to perceive the lamps and begin to clear the way
param_proposals.source: driver-response studies of emergency-vehicle encounters (perception-reaction time plus lane-change time)

segmentation.text: Upon the immediate approach of
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency,
making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of every other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Stop and remain in such position until the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle has passed.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'; conduct carried by u4 and u1.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'every other' excludes the approaching vehicle; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; read with role police_officer governing a travel region the subject occupies.

'Stop': DEF-NRS-484A-255 ('when required, means complete cessation from movement'), the concept drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement'). 'remain in such position': 'such position' is the position paragraph (b) describes, 'parallel to, and as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or, if applicable, curb of a highway and clear of any intersection', off a shoulder whose signage allows listed vehicles to use it; it is carried in full: heading (kin.heading) parallel to the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of an occupied (rel.occupies) travel region (st.travel_region); body within the edge gap (st.region_geometry ground distance) of a st.road_edge region ('curb or edge of the roadway') on its right (prim.region_lateral_offset at most zero) lying (st.on_way) on the highway (st.highway) it is on, or on a paved st.shoulder; overlapping no st.intersection; and overlapping no paved shoulder that a shoulder_use_permitted dev.regulatory_sign governs (dev.governs). 'until ... has passed': the approaching vehicle has gone past the subject, the subject lying behind it in its frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component negative) with their projections on its heading sharing no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); the 'not a stand-in' clauses of rel.longitudinal_overlap (neither a contact nor a distance) are respected, it is read only as the projection overlap.

operationalizations.standard: the immediate approach of the emergency or regulatory vehicle
operationalizations.convention: the vehicle moves with the subject ahead of it in its own frame, within the centre distance a vehicle at an urban response speed covers in the time a driver needs to perceive its lamps and begin clearing the way

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

applicability: For some road user e, not the subject, the trigger rises at this observation (holds here, not at the previous observation): e is of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject ahead of it in its frame, within centre distance p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach; and no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: For every e whose trigger rises here, with Passed(e) = (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from e to the subject negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap of e and the subject negative) and AtPosition = (drv.motion.complete_halt of the subject with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance; its heading's absolute dot product with the designated direction of a travel region it occupies at least p.curb_parallel_cos; for some highway h on which an occupied travel region lies, a road_edge region lying on h within ground distance p.pullover_edge_gap of its body with prim.region_lateral_offset at most zero, or a paved shoulder lying on h that it occupies; no intersection region occupied; no paved shoulder governed by a shoulder_use_permitted regulatory sign occupied): (not Passed(e)) strong-until (AtPosition and (AtPosition strong-until Passed(e))). The subject comes to rest at the position before e passes and stays at rest there until e has passed.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'such position' is carried with every qualification of paragraph (b), its 'as close as possible' read through the same edge gap as NRS_484B_267_1b_o1; the stop must come before the vehicle passes, so a subject still slowing when it passes has not stopped; a vehicle that never passes leaves the duty open until the trace ends (unknown)

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The trigger rises as ambulance e with a lit red flashing front lamp closes from behind; the subject pulls to the right edge and comes to rest there (AtPosition), then moves off again while e is still behind it (the subject ahead of e in e's frame) and before e passes.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject comes to rest at the right road_edge within p.pullover_edge_gap, parallel within p.curb_parallel_cos, clear of intersections, and stays at rest until e has gone past (the subject behind e, longitudinal overlap negative).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e approaches with its warning lamps off: the trigger never rises.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the trigger rose is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject comes to rest in the middle of its lane, far from any road_edge region, and stays at rest until e passes: it stopped and remained, but not in such position.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject keeps moving and e passes it before the subject has come to rest anywhere.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
at:
A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: Mapping index: 'It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate' maps to kin.speed. To drive or operate is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, and the prohibited driving is driving at a speed: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s.
Mapping index: 'a vehicle of any kind or character' maps to the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate', never expanded into classes.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: stopping-sight-distance model (perception-reaction distance plus braking distance at the friction-limited deceleration of the surface) held within the distance available ahead: the sight distance of the place, the visibility of the air and, in darkness, the low-beam reach; for traffic, the assured-clear-distance model against the road user ahead in the lane, whose own braking distance is credited; for curves, the side-friction model (speed squared times curvature within the lateral acceleration the surface allows); for width, the time-to-line-crossing model (lateral drift at the uncorrected heading error times the speed, within the lateral margin the lane leaves the vehicle, for at least the minimum time to line crossing)

applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving: kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance.
obligation: With v the subject's speed, a the braking deceleration the surface allows (p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds; otherwise p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds; otherwise p.following_decel_dry: a Term.cond selection), and S = v·p.driver_reaction_time + v·v/(2a): (i) S is at most st.sight_distance at the subject's place and at most env.visibility, and, where env.darkness holds, at most p.low_beam_sight_reach; (ii) for every road user u ahead of the subject in its lane, whatever its class (DEF-NRS-484A-285 'traffic' counts 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances' using the highway, so any road user ahead in the lane is traffic) (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), S is at most rel.surface_gap between them plus u's braking distance (u's speed squared over 2a); (iii) v·v·st.curvature at the subject's place is at most p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds and p.curve_lateral_accel_max otherwise; (iv) for every lane the subject's footprint overlaps, v·p.lane_keeping_heading_error·p.lane_departure_time_min is at most half of (st.lane_width of that lane minus the subject's width from kin.extent). No division reads a measured atom.

narrowings.why: 'drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it

the standard is the whole duty and is read through a policy model (surrogate): 'the traffic' only through the road users ahead in the subject's lane (crossing and adjacent traffic not read); 'surface' through wet and icy or snow-covered surface; 'width of the highway' through the width of the lane the subject occupies; 'the weather' through precipitation and visibility; the catch-all 'other highway conditions' only through sight distance, curvature and darkness, and no other condition

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry daylight road, the subject moving on a straight lane wide enough for it, no road user ahead; its speed is such that v·p.driver_reaction_time + v·v/(2·p.following_decel_dry) exceeds st.sight_distance at its place (a blind crest ahead).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Dry daylight road, straight wide lane, no road user ahead, a long st.sight_distance and env.visibility; the subject moves at a speed whose stopping distance is within them and whose lateral drift bound holds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject stands at rest (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.sight_distance is not observed on the source, and every other bound holds, so the verdict turns on the missing sight distance.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: env.ice_or_snow holds; the subject moves at a speed whose stopping distance on dry pavement would fit st.sight_distance but whose stopping distance with p.following_decel_ice exceeds it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Dry road, ample sight, but on a bend where v·v·st.curvature exceeds p.curve_lateral_accel_max.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A road user u is ahead in the subject's lane, nearly stopped, and the subject's stopping distance exceeds the surface gap plus u's braking distance.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
param_proposals.source: Johansson and Rumar brake-reaction studies; AASHTO Green Book

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: tyre-pavement friction tables (AASHTO; accident-reconstruction handbooks)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: tyre-pavement friction tables (AASHTO; accident-reconstruction handbooks)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: tyre-pavement friction tables (AASHTO; accident-reconstruction handbooks)

param_proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel_max
param_proposals.convention: the lateral acceleration a passenger vehicle sustains on a curve within comfortable side friction on a dry or wet paved surface (about 0.3 g)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book side-friction factors for horizontal curves

param_proposals.name: p.lane_keeping_heading_error
param_proposals.convention: the sine of the heading error (about 1.7 degrees) that a driver's lane keeping leaves uncorrected, so that the vehicle drifts laterally at that fraction of its speed
param_proposals.source: lane-keeping and time-to-line-crossing studies (Godthelp)

param_proposals.name: p.lane_departure_time_min
param_proposals.convention: the shortest time to line crossing a driver tolerates before correcting its lateral drift: the warning threshold of lane-departure warning systems
param_proposals.source: ISO 17361 lane departure warning systems

param_proposals.name: p.low_beam_sight_reach
param_proposals.convention: the distance ahead a passenger-car low beam lights the road in darkness enough to see an obstacle
param_proposals.source: UNECE R112 / SAE J1383 low-beam photometry

segmentation.text: Upon approaching
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency
which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Decrease the speed of his or her vehicle
to a speed that is reasonable and proper, pursuant to the criteria set forth in subsection 1 of NRS 484B.600 [NRS-484B-600-1a].

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'approaching' the emergency vehicle: the subject moves (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above the halt tolerance) with the emergency vehicle ahead of it in its own frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive), within the centre distance (rel.centre_distance 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') at which its lamps engage the approaching driver. rel.centre_distance's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival') is respected: it only bounds the range of the approach.

Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'; its conduct is carried by t4 and t6.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

'moving': the emergency vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance. 'preparing to move', as t12 defines it, 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver ... including ... (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver': sig.hand_signal 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}' with a meaning other than no_signal, or sig.turn_indicator 'state in {off, left, right}' other than off (a further visible indication of the open list; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' respected: it is read as the indication, not the move), with the emergency vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible 'b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight').

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'any other' excludes the emergency vehicle itself; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; read with role police_officer governing a travel region the subject occupies.

'Decrease the speed': kin.accel_longitudinal 'acceleration along heading, signed', at or below minus the deceleration resolution at some observation of the approach before the subject draws level with the emergency vehicle; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: speed' is respected: the decrease is the deceleration, the reached speed is t11's composition. Drawing level: rel.longitudinal_overlap 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)' at or above zero; read only as that projection, as its contract requires.

The definition of 'preparing to move' used by t4: 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver' (rel.visible from the subject to the emergency vehicle) 'that ... is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle' (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) 'or (b) The use of hand signals' (sig.hand_signal other than no_signal); the open list is also read through sig.turn_indicator other than off.

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: illustrative: arriving at or leaving a scene are instances of moving or preparing to move, which t4 already reads; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving a scene

applicability: There is a road user e, not the subject, of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, showing a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (visible from the subject, rel.visible, with a hand signal other than no_signal or a turn indicator other than off); the subject is approaching e: it moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), e lies ahead of it in its frame (rel.bearing longitudinal positive), their centre distance is at most p.emergency_approach_reach, and they are not side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative). And no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: (i) The subject complies with NRS_484B_600_1a at this observation (rule composition, subject to subject). (ii) For every such e whose condition rises at this observation (holds here, not at the previous observation): (rel.longitudinal_overlap of the subject and e negative) strong-until (kin.accel_longitudinal of the subject at or below minus p.speed_decrease_decel_min): the subject decelerates before it draws level with e.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move' is defined (t12) as an indication 'visible to an approaching driver': read as the emergency vehicle being visible from the subject (rel.visible) while it gives the indication

'decrease the speed' is read as a deceleration beyond the source's resolution at some observation after the approach begins and before the subject draws level; a subject that never draws level and never decelerates leaves this part unknown at the end of the trace

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Ambulance e, moving, with a lit red flashing front lamp, is ahead of the moving subject within p.emergency_approach_reach; the subject holds a constant speed (kin.accel_longitudinal near zero) until its body overlaps e longitudinally.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the subject decelerates beyond p.speed_decrease_decel_min before drawing level, and its speed meets every bound of NRS_484B_600_1a.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e's warning lamps are off (no lit sig.warning_lamp) as the subject approaches.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the duty is engaged is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject decelerates before drawing level, but its speed still exceeds the stopping-sight bound of NRS_484B_600_1a on a wet road.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: e stands at rest with its lamps flashing, gives no hand signal and its turn indicator is off: it is neither moving nor preparing to move.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: e stands at rest with lamps flashing and is visible from the subject, its driver giving a hand signal (preparing to move); the subject draws level without decelerating.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow
param_proposals.source: emergency warning-light conspicuity studies; move-over law guidance

param_proposals.name: p.speed_decrease_decel_min
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration at or beyond which a sampled acceleration counts as a decrease of speed rather than noise or rolling resistance: the acceleration resolution of the source
param_proposals.source: vehicle-state estimation noise of the acquisition standard

segmentation.text: Upon approaching
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency
which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Proceed
with caution.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'approaching' the emergency vehicle: the subject moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) with the emergency vehicle ahead in its frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive), within the centre distance (rel.centre_distance 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') at which its lamps engage the driver; rel.centre_distance is not used as a clearance or an order of arrival.

Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'; its conduct is carried by t4 and t6.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

'moving': the emergency vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance. 'preparing to move', as t12 defines it: sig.hand_signal 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {no_signal, ...}' other than no_signal, or sig.turn_indicator other than off (read as the indication, not the move it precedes), with the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible 'an unobstructed line of sight').

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'any other' excludes the emergency vehicle itself; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; read with role police_officer governing a travel region the subject occupies.
'Proceed': the subject continues to move, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above the halt tolerance; the manner of proceeding is the standard t11.

The definition of 'preparing to move' used by t4: 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver' (rel.visible) 'that ... is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle' (kin.speed) 'or (b) The use of hand signals' (sig.hand_signal); the open list also read through sig.turn_indicator.

operationalizations.convention: caution is read through the conduct it secures toward the emergency vehicle: no traffic-conflict with it (closest approach of the centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision threshold below the collision clearance), no contact, and, while side by side with it, a gap between bodies of at least the lateral passing clearance

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: illustrative: arriving at or leaving a scene are instances of moving or preparing to move, which t4 already reads; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving a scene

applicability: There is a road user e, not the subject, of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, showing a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (visible from the subject, rel.visible, with a hand signal other than no_signal or a turn indicator other than off); the subject is approaching e: it moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), e lies ahead of it in its frame (rel.bearing longitudinal positive) or the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), and their centre distance is at most p.emergency_approach_reach. And no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: For every such e: the subject and e are not in contact; it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; and where rel.longitudinal_overlap of the subject and e is at or above zero, rel.surface_gap between them is at least p.emergency_pass_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move' is defined (t12) as an indication 'visible to an approaching driver': read as the emergency vehicle being visible from the subject (rel.visible) while it gives the indication
caution, a standard of the driver's care, is read only through the clearance the subject keeps from the emergency vehicle; its speed is judged by NRS_484B_267_2a

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Ambulance e, moving with a lit red flashing front lamp, is ahead of the moving subject within p.emergency_approach_reach; the subject passes alongside it with rel.surface_gap below p.emergency_pass_clearance while rel.longitudinal_overlap is at or above zero.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the subject passes with a gap of at least p.emergency_pass_clearance and no closest-approach conflict or contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e's warning lamps are off as the subject approaches and passes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the duty is engaged is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject closes on e from behind in its lane; their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: e stands at rest with its lamps flashing, no hand signal and no turn indicator: it is neither moving nor preparing to move.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow
param_proposals.source: emergency warning-light conspicuity studies; move-over law guidance

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hyden; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_pass_clearance
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies a driver keeps while passing alongside an emergency or enforcement vehicle: a lateral passing clearance of about half a lane's free width, leaving room for its crew and doors
param_proposals.source: lateral passing-clearance conventions of driver manuals and move-over guidance
